verdict.summary: Works for you and up to 100 test users within an hour, but test tokens die after 7 days. Reading email uses restricted scopes, which need Google verification plus a paid third-party security assessment (CASA) that repeats every 12 months. Your scope choice decides whether this takes days or months.

time_to_first_connection.basis: Estimate: create Cloud project, configure consent screen in Testing, create web client, add yourself as a test user.

time_to_production.estimate: 2–5 days (non-sensitive) · ~1–2 weeks (sensitive) · several weeks to months (restricted)
time_to_production.basis: Google: brand verification 2–3 days; sensitive scopes 3–5 business days on one page, 10 days on another; restricted 'can potentially take several weeks'. CASA budgeting from a third party: 10–20 days. Community reports of stalls.

top_blockers: Restricted Gmail scopes require a CASA security assessment by a Google-approved assessor, renewed yearly
Testing mode: 100-user cap and refresh tokens that expire after 7 days
Scopes in your code that don't match the consent screen trigger the unverified-app screen

key_decision.question: Which Gmail scopes do you actually need?
key_decision.recommendation: Use the narrowest scope that delivers your feature. Sending only? gmail.send is sensitive, not restricted. Reading the inbox is restricted and brings CASA.
key_decision.why: Google groups scopes into non-sensitive, sensitive and restricted. Restricted adds a security assessment if data touches your servers. One team in the community dropped gmail.readonly to escape CASA.

prerequisites.item: Google account and a Google Cloud project
Verified domain, homepage and privacy policy that mention your Google data use
Budget for a CASA assessment (restricted scopes only)

steps.title: Classify your scopes
steps.detail: List the Gmail scopes your features need, mark each non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted, and suggest narrower ones (for example gmail.send instead of a read scope).

steps.title: Create a dedicated Cloud project
steps.detail: Verification and scopes are project-wide, so don't share a project with unrelated apps.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API and configure the consent screen
steps.detail: The consent screen now lives under 'Google Auth Platform' in the console. Set User type External, Publishing status Testing.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: Add your redirect URIs and store the client secret securely.

steps.title: Add up to 100 test users
steps.detail: In Testing, only listed test users can authorize. Their authorizations and refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and privacy-policy text
steps.detail: Write a justification for each scope, the privacy-policy section about Google user data, and the demo video script for the verification submission.

steps.title: Publish the app and submit for verification
steps.detail: Click Publish app, then use the Verification Center. Declare every scope with justification and a demo video.

steps.title: Brand verification
steps.detail: Google checks logo, display name, URLs and domain ownership.

steps.title: Sensitive/restricted scope review
steps.detail: Google checks use case, limited use and minimum scopes.

steps.title: CASA security assessment (restricted only)
steps.detail: Final step. Google's Trust & Safety team contacts you when it's time. Done by a Google-empanelled assessor using the App Defense Alliance CASA framework; you get a Letter of Validation.

steps.title: Re-assess every 12 months
steps.detail: Restricted-scope apps must re-verify and repeat the assessment at least yearly.

nuances.title: 7-day token expiry in Testing
nuances.detail: Looks like a working integration, then breaks a week later. Exception: apps requesting only openid/email/profile.

nuances.title: 100-user cap applies even after publishing
nuances.detail: An unverified app requesting sensitive or restricted scopes is capped at 100 users total and shows the unverified-app warning.

nuances.title: Adding a scope later restarts review
nuances.detail: Using a new sensitive scope before approval brings back the unverified screen and 100-user cap.

nuances.title: Internal (Workspace-only) apps
nuances.detail: Apps limited to your own Google Workspace org may avoid verification. Not confirmed in sources checked today.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'Google hasn't verified this app'
blockers.cause: Requesting sensitive/restricted scopes not yet approved, or code scopes don't match the consent screen
blockers.fix: Align code and consent screen scopes; submit for verification.
Reply on the last email thread from the verification team; state any scopes you removed.
Publish to production (and verify if needed).

agent_can: Classify each scope you need as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted and suggest narrower alternatives
Draft scope justifications, privacy-policy sections about Google data, and the demo video script
you_must: Create the project and consent screen while signed in
Choose and pay a CASA assessor and fix their findings

corrected: Google's own pages disagree on sensitive-scope review time: 3–5 business days (developer docs) vs 10 days (help center table). The guide shows the range.
unverified: CASA cost: not published by Google.
Internal-user-type exemption not confirmed in today's sources.
'Google Auth Platform' console renaming comes from a third party.
